title: When AI-assisted criticism scales, peer review needs an obligation threshold - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A Nature Machine Intelligence comment (preview only; full text paywalled) by Sun, Li, Lee and Chen argues that AI makes generating referee criticism nearly free while evaluating it stays expensive, shifting peer review's bottleneck to judging which concerns matter and requiring an 'obligation threshold' for which concerns authors must address.

insights.claim: AI assistance lets a peer-review referee produce large volumes of manuscript-specific feedback in seconds, while judging whether any given concern changes a paper's central claim still requires substantial expert attention.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Generation of AI critique is commoditizing; expert judgment is not — watch where scarce human evaluation capacity becomes the bottleneck.

insights.claim: AI changes the economics of peer review because the marginal cost of raising a plausible concern falls much faster than the cost of evaluating what should follow from that concern.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Asymmetric cost curves (cheap generation, expensive verification) are a general pattern for AI in knowledge work and favour tools that triage rather than generate.
insights.quote: the marginal cost of raising a plausible concern can fall much faster than the cost of evaluating what should follow from that concern

insights.claim: The scarce resource in scientific peer review may shift from generating criticism to judging which criticism matters.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Value in research-integrity and editorial tooling may migrate toward prioritization/filtering of AI-generated critique.
insights.quote: The scarce resource in peer review may consequently shift from generating criticism to judging which criticism matters

themes.theme: Authority of referee concerns and the obligation threshold

insights.claim: In peer review, concerns raised in a referee report carry authority: authors are typically expected either to address them or to explain why they have not, so they rarely remain neutral observations.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Each added AI-generated concern imposes a response burden on authors, inflating review cycles and costs for publishers and researchers.
insights.quote: In peer review, criticism carries authority.
insights.locator: In peer review, criticism carries authority.

insights.claim: The time and attention needed to formulate manuscript-specific concerns historically capped how many concerns a referee could raise, and AI weakens this natural constraint — motivating the authors' call for an 'obligation threshold' defining which concerns authors must answer.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Expect journals (e.g., Nature Portfolio titles) to adopt policies on AI-assisted reviewing and limits on which critiques require response; relevant to scholarly publishers like Springer Nature.
